title: Controlling how tests are run
summary: Command-line options for cargo test: running tests in parallel or one at a time, showing output, running a subset by name, ignoring slow tests, and the two kinds of arguments.

sections: TRPL 11.2 Controlling How Tests Are Run
TRPL 11.2 Running Tests in Parallel or Consecutively
TRPL 11.2 Running a Subset of Tests by Name
TRPL 11.2 Ignoring Tests Unless Specifically Requested

blocks.md:
`cargo test` compiles your code in test mode and runs the resulting binary. Some options go to Cargo, others to the test binary. They are separated by `--`:

```bash
cargo test --release -- --test-threads=1
#          ^ for cargo   ^ for the test binary
```

`cargo test --help` lists the first kind, `cargo test -- --help` the second.

blocks.title: Parallel or one at a time
blocks.md:
By default tests run **in parallel** on several threads, which is fast. It means tests must not depend on each other or on shared state, such as a file they all write to. If they do, either make each test use its own resources (a unique file name) or run them on one thread:

```bash
cargo test -- --test-threads=1
```

blocks.title: Showing output
blocks.md:
For passing tests, the test runner **captures** anything printed with `println!` and throws it away, so the report stays readable. For a failing test, its output is shown in the failure section. To see output from passing tests too:

```bash
cargo test -- --show-output
```

(`--nocapture` also shows output, as it happens, interleaved between threads.)

blocks.title: Only one filter
blocks.md: You can pass only one name filter to `cargo test`. To pick several unrelated tests, choose a common part of their names, or run them separately.

blocks.title: Ignoring slow tests

blocks.code:
$ cargo test
running 2 tests
test tests::expensive_test ... ignored, takes about a minute
test tests::it_works ... ok

test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.00s

$ cargo test -- --ignored            # only the ignored ones
$ cargo test -- --include-ignored    # everything

questions.q: Two tests write to the same file `out.txt` and fail randomly. What is the quick fix?
questions.explanation: Running on one thread removes the race; a better fix is separate files.

questions.explanation: The double dash separates the two.

questions.q: How do you run tests marked `#[ignore]`?

points: Options before `--` go to Cargo, options after it to the test binary.
Tests run in parallel; keep them independent or use `--test-threads=1`.
Output of passing tests is captured; show it with `--show-output`.
`cargo test name` filters by substring; `#[ignore]` skips slow tests until `--ignored`.

terms.def: A name fragment passed to cargo test so only matching tests run.
An attribute that skips a test unless cargo test is run with --ignored or --include-ignored.
The test runner hiding stdout of passing tests to keep the report short.
